The authors’ [BERT4Rec generator](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/gen_data.py) implements random masking and forced-last masking; its [loss implementation](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/run.py) averages over all valid masked targets across the batch. [Recency Sampling](https://arxiv.org/html/2207.02643) studies exponential position weights and ablates recency strength, but removes sampled targets and evaluates other architectures against BERT4Rec. These sources do not establish an isolated BERT4Rec terminal-masking × endpoint-recency ablation or a validated 10-interaction half-life.

For a reproducible proposed adaptation, uniformly sample an eligible user, then sample endpoint t∈{2,…,n} from training-only history with P(t)∝2^{−(n−t)/10}; equivalently α=2^{−1/10}≈0.9330. Sample before context truncation. With total token capacity L, terminal input is left_pad(last_{L−1}(x₁,…,x_{t−1})+[MASK], L), label x_t. Never include the target occurrence or interactions after t; earlier legitimate repetitions may remain. Inference uses the identical truncation and appended mask, reading its final position. For reconstruction, truncate a training-only prefix, select nonpadding targets, and replace every selected occurrence with MASK—avoiding unchanged-target corruption. Specify masking probability, ensure at least one target, and fix terminal-example probability q independently of endpoint sampling.

Per-example normalization is mean_b[(1/m_b)Σ_jℓ_bj]; per-target normalization is Σ_bjℓ_bj/Σ_bm_b. The latter gives examples with more reconstruction targets greater weight, so q no longer directly controls terminal loss contribution. Prefer per-example normalization when q should represent objective weight; report both as an ablation. Isolate effects with a 2×2 design: reconstruction-only versus terminal mixture, crossed with uniform versus exponential endpoints; hold truncation, seeds, optimizer, updates and validation evaluator fixed. These are proposed controls, not published findings.
